scope: Generic exact angular moments for independent occupied domains; isolated exploration
input: A monomial in upper-triangular spatial Gram entries q_i dot q_j, multiplied if needed by an arbitrary coefficient independent of the angular coordinates
factorization: Every vector q_i has a fixed homogeneous degree t_i in a Gram monomial. Its independent sphere average vanishes for odd t_i. Otherwise the result is product_i(r_i^2)^(t_i/2) times a rational function of the spatial dimension d. Energy variables remain untouched and may be carried by the coefficient.
identity: The normalized sphere moment of 2m components is r^(2m) times the sum of pairwise Kronecker contractions divided by d(d+2)...(d+2m-2). The formula follows by separating radius and direction in an isotropic Gaussian and continues meromorphically in d.
algorithm: Remove diagonal Gram factors and retain their contribution to the final radial powers. Eliminate the first remaining vector with off-diagonal factors.

Its neighbor multiplicities encode the labels of all tensor indices. Choose one occurrence of the first nonempty label. A partner label j has exactly the remaining multiplicity of j choices. Multiply the recursively grouped contraction by that multiplicity.

Contraction of two equal neighbor labels contributes a unit-sphere diagonal factor one; contraction of two distinct labels adds the corresponding Gram edge. Collect equal resulting multigraphs and cache them by the multiplicity vector.

Divide by the sphere denominator for the eliminated vector, then recursively average each resulting graph of the other independent vectors. Cache this average by the complete off-diagonal Gram exponent vector.

Return the original radial degrees and the exact rational function in d. The same procedure applies to any supported number of independent vectors; it contains no topology name, chosen invariant, or evaluated reference data.
limits: Explicit retained-cache and intermediate-map cardinality budgets, total-degree preflight at most 512, and checked u16 exponent/radial overflow; exploratory geometry arity at most 16. Host enforces polynomial-size, wall-time and serialized-byte limits separately. No polynomial-complexity claim for arbitrary high-degree coupled graphs.
verification: Odd independent parity and arbitrary diagonal radial factors
Coupled three-vector triangle and squared triangle, with exact symbolic d
Four-vector cycle, with exact symbolic d
Rank 128 at d=11/2, checked against the independent Gaussian double-factorial moment, retaining fewer than 200 cache entries
Degree preflight rejects near-u16-limit input before any recursive cache allocation
remaining_validation: The physical producer must cross-check this angular adapter against the existing native low-rank projector and combine it with the existing distributional radial moments; angular success alone makes no statement about C_n normalization, Fermi surfaces, equation reconstruction or eta=0 transport.
